newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African coke canner opens new 86 mln rand line.
newsitem.headline: S.African coke canner opens new 86 mln rand line.

text.p: South African canner Amalgamated Beverage Canners (ABC) on Thursday opened a new canning line that makes the firm's plant the largest Coca-Cola Co canning facility in the southern hemisphere and one of the top five biggest in the world.
The new hi-tech Line Five has the capacity to fill 2,000 cans a minute and should increase production at the plant, at Wadeville near Johannesburg, to 1.6 billion soft drinks a year.

ABC is 51 percent owned by Coca-Cola and 49 percent owned by South Africa's eight independent coke bottlers. The firm also operates canning plants in Pinetown in KwaZulu Natal and Epping in the Western Cape.

The opening ceremony for the new canning line was marked by a wildcat demonstration by factory workers, who gathered outside to protest for higher wages and for more affirmative action to promote black workers at ABC.
"Coke outside has a great image, but their workers are not very happy," said Loyiso Sikweze, acting chairman of the shop stewards' committee at the plant.
Sikweze said the protest had been organised internally and was not an official action of the Food and Allied Workers Union.
Coke management said they were caught unawares by the protest, but added that they were confident wage negotiations could be settled amicably.
"The differences, I don't think, are that big. We are confident we can work it out," said communications director Paul Pendergrass.
Pendergrass added that Coke was committed to giving opportunities to black workers. "The Coca-Cola system is committed to black empowerment at every level of the business," he said.
He pointed out that last week black investment group Kunene Brothers Holdings bought Coke's 13 percent stake in South African bottler Vinto Minerals.
The move brings Kunene's share of Vinto to 64 percent and the firm said it makes them the single largest individual black investor in the South African soft drinks industry.
The new line at ABC, which is to be renamed Coca-Cola Canners of South Africa, represents an 86 million rand ($18.7 million) investment.

But the line got off to a shaky start as dozens of cans were crushed in the machinery as production began. However, workers fixed a problem in the line's lubrication system and production restarted smoothly.
"Starting up is always difficult," said Hans Kaltenbrun, ABC general manager.

The plant has the capacity for additional volume if needed in the future and will serve the domestic South African market, as well as produce drinks for export to neighbouring countries in southern Africa such as Angola and Mozambique. ($ = 4.609 South African Rand)
